definitions: The portion of a distribution having a large number of occurrences far from the 'head' or central part of the distribution.

A business strategy allowing companies to realize significant profits by selling low volumes of hard-to-find items to many customers, instead of only selling large volumes of a reduced number of popular items.
examples: The company's success is attributed to its long tail strategy.
Understanding the long tail of consumer preferences is crucial.
Digital platforms often benefit from the long tail phenomenon.
